children: , the dominant artificial-intelligence accelerator supplier, climbed roughly 0.6% to $220.43 Friday, finding buyers after a bruising stretch against rival chipmakers. The shares had lost about 5% since Tuesday, Barron's reported, while AMD
advanced around 5%a striking performance gap of nearly ten percentage points.

Amazon's major AI-chip agreement with Qualcomm gave investors another reason to explore alternatives to Nvidia. Yet the financial scoreboard remains brutally one-sided. Nvidia produced $89 billion in data-center revenue during its fiscal second quarter, a 117% surge representing roughly 92.5% of total sales. Management now expects third-quarter revenue of approximately $108 billion.

The image reinforces that strength: Nvidia's 96-out-of-100 GF Score is powered by exceptional profitability, growth, financial strength and momentum, while GF Value remains the clear weak spot. That tension matters because Nvidia's $5.35 trillion market value equals roughly 13.9 times annualized second-quarter revenue. One rough week does not signal a competitive collapse, but it shows that investors are ready to reward credible challengers long before those rivals leave a visible mark on Nvidia's enormous AI business.

title: Nvidia Rebounds After Rivals Open a 10-Point Weekly Gap
